1.Nf3 d5 2.e3 Nf6 3.c4 e6 4.Nc3.strategy: Brings out the queenside knight to attack d5 a second time, so Black has to keep that pawn well guarded. White builds a classical set-up with c4 and e3 behind the pieces and keeps the d-pawn's advance in hand.

1.Nf3 d5 2.e3 Nf6 3.c4 e6 4.Nc3 Be7.strategy: Develops the bishop to a safe square behind the pawns and prepares castling, while d5 keeps its full support. Black does not need to hurry: the compact structure holds, and the one long-term worry is the c8-bishop behind e6.
